answer: DeepWalk tends to outperform LINE(2nd) on DBLP(PaperCitation) because its stochastic gradient descent is driven by random-walk contexts, which capture higher-order and more global network structure than LINE(2nd)’s purely second-order, local neighborhood objective. In practice, DeepWalk samples many short random walks and treats nodes that co-occur within a window as training pairs, so SGD sees a richer and more diverse set of positive examples, including nodes connected through multi-step paths. This helps it learn embeddings that preserve community and structural similarity better on citation networks like DBLP, where useful relationships are often not just immediate links but also indirect citation patterns. LINE(2nd), by contrast, mainly preserves second-order proximity from direct neighbors and their adjacency distributions, so it can miss some of the broader context that DeepWalk captures. The SGD itself is not the main reason by itself; rather, the combination of SGD with random-walk sampling and skip-gram-style training gives DeepWalk a more expressive training signal on this graph.
